- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — adjust for lagged momentum by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent price is rising.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 2–5% in the first 10 days; apply a 1–2% upward bias to early forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.2) followed by a price rise, model tends to miss the rally; anticipate 1–3% upward correction in next 3–5 days.
